subparts.derivation: det Σ=4-1=3 and Σ⁻¹=(1/3)[[2,-1],[-1,2]]. With a=x1-1,b=x2+1, the exponent is -(a²-ab+b²)/3. Expanding gives a²-ab+b²=x1²-x1x2+x2²-3x1+3x2+3.
subparts.checks: Σ≻0 since its first leading minor is 2 and determinant is 3. Normalizer follows (2π)^(-2/2)|Σ|^(-1/2), so integral=1; quadratic at μ=(1,-1) is 0.

subparts.derivation: 4z²-8z+7=4(z-1)²+3. Thus integral p=c e^(-3/2)∫exp[-2(z-1)²]dz=c e^(-3/2)√(π/2). Setting it to 1 yields c=e^(3/2)√(2/π). The exponent -2(z-1)² is -(z-1)²/(2·1/4).
subparts.checks: Normalized density becomes √(2/π) exp[-2(z-1)²], whose integral is 1. c alone is not the Gaussian prefactor until the e^(-3/2) term is combined.

subparts.derivation: Each independent residual εn=yn-θ0-θ1xn has density (2πσ²)^(-1/2)exp[-εn²/(2σ²)]. Multiply N densities: prefactors multiply to (2πσ²)^(-N/2), and exponent terms sum.
subparts.checks: Inputs are fixed, so this is the joint conditional data density as a function of parameters. σ²>0 ensures a positive finite normalizer.

subparts.derivation: The N-dimensional covariance determinant is (σ²)^N and inverse is I/σ². Taking minus the log of the Gaussian likelihood gives N log(2π)/2+N log(σ²)/2+||y-Φθ||²/(2σ²). The first terms are independent of θ and the SSE coefficient is positive.
subparts.checks: Φ:N×K, θ:K×1, y:N×1; the norm is scalar. Since log is strictly increasing and negation reverses order, the optimization equivalence holds even if the minimizer is not unique.

subparts.derivation: J=(y-Φθ)ᵀ(y-Φθ)=yᵀy-2θᵀΦᵀy+θᵀΦᵀΦθ. Because ΦᵀΦ is symmetric, ∇J=-2Φᵀy+2ΦᵀΦθ. Set to zero: ΦᵀΦθ=Φᵀy. For any nonzero v, vᵀΦᵀΦv=||Φv||²>0 under full column rank, so the matrix is invertible and Hessian 2ΦᵀΦ is positive definite.
subparts.checks: Gradient K×1 and Hessian K×K. Positive definiteness proves the unique global minimum, not merely stationarity.

subparts.derivation: Φ=[[1,-1],[1,0],[1,1]], ΦᵀΦ=diag(3,2), Φᵀy=(7,2)ᵀ. Solve to obtain (7/3,1)ᵀ. Predicted values are (7/3-1,7/3,7/3+1); residuals are (2/3,-4/3,2/3).

subparts.derivation: Bayes gives -log posterior=||y-Φθ||²/(2σ²)+||θ||²/(2b²)+constant independent of θ. Its gradient is (ΦᵀΦθ-Φᵀy)/σ²+θ/b². Multiplication by σ² and setting zero yields (ΦᵀΦ+(σ²/b²)I)θ=Φᵀy. Multiplying the objective by the positive 2σ² gives SSE+(σ²/b²)||θ||².
subparts.checks: λ>0. For v≠0, vᵀ(ΦᵀΦ+λI)v=||Φv||²+λ||v||²>0, so the inverse exists even without full rank. All coefficients, including the intercept, receive the penalty.

subparts.derivation: Σ0⁻¹=diag(1,1/2), Σ1⁻¹=(1/3)[[2,-1],[-1,2]]. Their sum H=[[5/3,-1/3],[-1/3,7/6]] has determinant 11/6. The linear term h=Σ0⁻¹μ0+Σ1⁻¹μ1=(1/3,1/3)ᵀ. Completing the square gives covariance C=H⁻¹=(1/11)[[7,2],[2,10]] and mean m=Ch=(3/11,4/11)ᵀ. With u=x1-3/11,v=x2-4/11, (x-m)ᵀH(x-m)=(5/3)u²-(2/3)uv+(7/6)v².
subparts.checks: HC=I2 and Hm=h exactly. det C=6/11, so normalizer=(2π)^(-1)(det C)^(-1/2)=√(11/6)/(2π). H11=5/3>0 and det H=11/6>0 prove integrability and positive covariance; the normalized Gaussian integral is 1.
